pages.title: Amber Nautilus
pages.text:
Concentric rings of amber and teal spiral inward toward a luminous cyan vortex, the whole figure turning like a chambered shell cut in half. The square-dither perturbation roughens the ring edges into beaded chains, and the zzold feedback transform layers each step’s history into the next. The centroid-distance metric colors each solve by how far its root cloud center sits from the origin — the outermost rings are farthest, glowing gold; the inner spiral is closest, shining cyan. The reef palette completes the oceanic illusion.

pages.title: Crown of Thorns
pages.text:
A single rust-and-ember crown floats in a vast field of concentric brown ripples, its circumference dotted with small dark voids like thorns worked into the metal. Seventy roots per solve sweep around the unit circle through the swirler coefficient transform and reversal — the swirler twists the coefficient vector like taffy before the reversal folds it back on itself. The clusteriness score at a tight 1.5 percent clip lights up where the nearest neighbors pack most densely, and the desert-warmwhite-ember tri-palette paints the crown in ember and the surrounding rings in burnt umber. The dark perforations are the solve points where no root cluster ever forms, small holes burned into the metal band.

pages.title: Magenta Galaxy
pages.text:
A swirling galactic vortex of magenta and silver dust spirals around a hollow violet core, rendered from the same p11b3 polynomial family that produced earlier passes from this compute job. Ten roots per solve are pushed through the roots5 parameter transform — a fifth-root lattice that fractures the smooth coefficient sweep into discrete spiral arms — and an autolevels pass pulls every filament out of the shadows. The composition reads as a long-exposure photograph of a slowly rotating galactic disc: dark hollow core, dense inner spiral, faint silver outer arms dissolving into the void.

pages.title: Bauhaus Bullseye
pages.text:
A luminous solar bullseye: a red pupil at the center, ringed by concentric bands of yellow, olive, and amber, the whole orb surrounded by a bristling corona of fine radial spikes that taper to the outer darkness. Seventy roots per solve from the creative10 function are pushed through the zzold parameter transform that feeds each step's output back as the next step's input, then resolved by the companion-matrix eigensolver so every eigenvalue lands exactly. The nearest-neighbor variation score at a five percent clip lights up where each root's closest sibling keeps changing identity, and the long Bauhaus shapes palette — thirteen primary hues in the spirit of the Weimar masters — paints the shells in hot yellows and reds against a cool olive backdrop. A resized print of an autolevels original, every band a frequency of the same underlying root cloud.

pages.title: Rust Iris
pages.text:
A turquoise aperture rings a cloud of rust and amber dust, the whole figure suspended on a faint halo of concentric ripples. The creative9 coefficient function with an eleven-parameter vector is pushed through a zero-one parameter warp and a sixth-coefficient twist, then the coefficients are run through a sort-cumulative-sum scramble that layers the orderings on top of each other. The outlierness score at a five-percent clip lights up the roots that stray farthest from the median radial distance, and the reef palette frames the burning interior with a cool teal eye-ring. At the center a dark pupil opens onto the void where all ten roots cluster near coincidence.

pages.title: Aureate Egg
pages.text:
A luminous torus of teal and gold cradles a braided interior of amber curtains and folded coefficient-space geometry — a cosmic egg with its shell peeled back to reveal the nested spirals inside. Thirty-four roots per solve are pushed through the unit-circle parameter sweep and a second-coefficient transform, then reversed at the coefficient stage. The outlierness score at a five-percent clip picks out the roots that wander farthest from the median radial distance, and the reef palette flares cyan where the shell thins and amber where it thickens. Above the egg, faint spines radiate outward — the signature of roots that briefly escaped before the solver caught them and pulled them back.

pages.title: Cerulean Owl
pages.text:

Thirty-five roots per solve sweep around the unit circle through a second-coefficient warp, then reverse at the coefficient stage to enforce the bilateral symmetry. The outlierness score at a five-percent clip picks out the structural outliers — the roots that drift farthest from their siblings' median radius — and the bwred palette stains the horned silhouette in icy blue with flashes of coral where the shell ruptures. Same uncanny portrait as Spectral Owl, painted in a cooler hand.

pages.title: Triquetra
pages.text:
Three translucent teal circles overlap in a perfect trefoil, their intersections darkening to indigo, with a small amber sun burning at the geometric center. Thirty-four roots per solve are swept around the unit circle through a seventh-coefficient transform, then reversed — a structural recipe that locks in the three-lobed rotational symmetry. The shelliness score measures how uniformly roots distribute around their centroid, and the reef palette paints the uniform shells in cool cyan and the amber pistil where the shell collapses to a point. A wide twenty-times square extent pulls the full orbital structure into view. The effect is a Celtic knot rendered from root orbits.

The proximity score at a tight 0.1% clip with omega enabled lights up where the nearest pair of roots comes closest to collision, and the reef palette traces the collision seams in cyan and the relaxed arcs in amber. The proximity score at a tight 0.1% clip with omega enabled lights up the tightest near-collisions, and the rainbow_d3 palette wraps D3's smooth rainbow gradient around the density gradient. The dark pupil at the center is unchanged — it is the structural void where no roots land regardless of the metric. This pair of images, Abyssal Iris and Unit Circle Scar, demonstrates how the same root cloud tells completely different stories depending on which geometric property you measure.

pages.title: Shattered Chrysanthemum
pages.text: Two interleaving complex exponential spirals — one tracing the sum of the parameters, the other their product — weave a field of degree-ten polynomials whose coefficients orbit the unit circle. The companion matrix eigenvalue transform then shatters each smooth spiral into algebraic fragments, scattering roots outward in a halo of lavender shards. Roots that cluster near the unit circle glow gold; those flung into the periphery cool to ink and violet. The result reads as a detonating flower: a molten chrysanthemum whose petals have been torn free and flung into the dark, trailing filaments of gold dust, while at the center a single bright point remains — the quiet eye of a mathematical storm.

pages.title: Shattered Aqua Supernova
pages.text: A dense, glowing red-orange core radiates outward into a chaotic, explosive halo of shattered aqua, teal, and gold. The central hub is tightly structured, resembling a delicate floral mandala, while the surrounding field fractures into thousands of sharp, sweeping shards that dissolve into the black void. Ten roots per solve from the giga_138 polynomial family are driven through a heavy stack of coefficient transforms—a cumulative sum followed by a power(2) squaring operation—which shatters the normally smooth root paths into this fragmented debris. The clusteriness metric, clipped at a tight three percent, maps the density of these root clusters. The retro brown-aqua tri-palette paints the highly clustered, stable center in warm reds and oranges, while the scattered, low-density outer fragments are cast in vibrant aquas and greens. An autolevels pass ensures even the faintest peripheral shards emerge clearly from the dark background, resolved by the multi-threaded Aberth solver.

pages.title: Aqua Ember Crescent
pages.text: A glowing crescent of fiery reds and warm yellows wraps around a dark central void, its surface studded with brilliant aqua nodes like jewels set in a burning horseshoe. Ten roots per solve from the giga_138 function are heavily warped by a sequence of coefficient transforms—sorting by absolute value, then applying inverse fourth-power and eighth-power functions—which fractures the typical circular symmetry into this open, U-shaped nebula. The multithreaded Aberth solver resolves the roots, while the shelliness metric evaluates how tightly the resulting clouds organize into concentric layers, clipped at a tight 3.0 percent to isolate the most structured regions. These highly organized clusters are painted in striking cyan by the retro brown and aqua tri-palette, while the looser, wispy filaments burn in intense crimson and gold. A final autolevels pass pulls the faintest fiery tendrils out of the deep black background, completing the illusion of a cosmic wreath ablaze in the dark.

pages.title: Reef Heart Nebula
pages.text: A luminous, heart-shaped nebula of cyan and gold dominates the dark void, its core a spinning vortex of fine golden threads. Smaller, delicate spiral eddies float like tiny galaxies in the surrounding space. Ten roots per solve from the giga_138 function are subjected to a rigorous sequence of coefficient transforms—an absolute-value sort, a fourth-order inverse power, a swirler, and a second fourth-order inverse power pass. This intense twisting and scaling of the coefficient vector fractures the root paths into intricate, fractal-like whorls. The outlierness metric at a tight three percent clip highlights the roots that sit furthest from their local clusters, painting the most isolated points in bright cyan and the denser, swirling structures in warm gold using the oceanic reef palette. The Aberth-Ehrlich solver resolves these heavily manipulated polynomials into a delicate, glowing web.

pages.title: Yarn Vortex
pages.text: A swirling, tangled mass of fine, hair-like filaments in magenta, cyan, and pale yellow, resembling a ball of spun glass or a complex nebula against a black void. Smaller vortexes and loops emerge from the main structure, twisting inward toward a dark, hollow core. Fourteen roots per solve sweep around the unit circle parameter transform, fed into the giga_139 polynomial function. The code's internal logic, explicitly designed to create "balls with holes," injects sudden jumps into the coefficient vector at two dynamically chosen positions, causing the smooth sweeps to fracture into these tangled, overlapping loops. The outlierness metric at a tight 3.0 percent clip highlights the most isolated root clusters, while the tri-warhol-marilyn-cyan palette paints the dense inner tangles in deep magenta and the sweeping outer filaments in cyan and pale yellow. The Aberth multithreaded solver resolves the chaotic threads into a cohesive, luminous web, capturing every delicate loop and whorl of the mathematical yarn.

pages.title: Magenta Shrapnel Ring
pages.text: A bristling corona of hot pink and magenta surrounds a dark, hollow core, exploding outward into a chaotic field of sharp cyan and gold needles. The texture resembles metallic shavings or high-speed fiber optics caught mid-detonation. Fourteen roots per solve from the giga_139 function—which explicitly carves "balls with holes" by injecting modulo-based anomalies into its coefficient array—create the central void. These roots are pushed through the roots6 parameter transform, while an inverse-power-of-four and a reversal coefficient transform violently stretch and fold the polynomial space, fracturing the outer edges into sharp, radiating splinters. The outlierness metric at a tight three percent clip isolates the most mathematically distant roots, mapping the dense inner ring to the hot pinks of the Warhol Marilyn Cyan tri-palette and painting the scattered outer spikes in bright cyan and gold. The multi-threaded Aberth solver resolves the chaotic field, leaving a luminous, jagged ring suspended in the dark.

pages.title: Fauvist Corona
pages.text: A central black void anchors a delicate, radiating sunburst of fine red and yellow filaments. These spokes extend outward to support a thick, undulating ring of luminous green, cyan, and pale yellow, resembling draped silk or an auroral corona. The outer edge of this ring flares into jagged, wing-like protrusions that dissolve into the grainy black background. Thirty-five roots per solve are generated by the poly_1 function, where trigonometric and logarithmic terms build the underlying structure. The parameters sweep along the unit_circle before the rev transform reverses the coefficient array, effectively turning the polynomial inside out and pushing the dense root clusters to the perimeter. The aberth_mt solver resolves the roots, which are then scored by the t1_re metric, mapping the real component of the first parameter to the vibrant tri_fauvism_wild palette. This specific color mapping paints the delicate inner radial lines in warm reds and the chaotic, folded outer perimeter in brilliant, electric greens, creating a striking contrast between the rigid inner geometry and the organic outer flares.

pages.title: Iron Gear
pages.text: A jagged, gear-like ring of bright orange, cream, and dark grey encircles a vast, smoky central void, while fine, hair-like filaments radiate outward from the ring's serrated edges into the surrounding darkness. Thirty-five roots per solve are generated by the poly_1 function, pushing the parameters through the zz3 transform and a power coefficient transform before the Aberth-Ehrlich solver resolves the polynomial. The clusteriness metric, clipped at a tight 0.1 percent, highlights regions where the roots pack most densely, painting the structure with the long Marvel Ironman palette. A sawtooth modifier repeats the color gradient ten times, creating the banded, concentric stripes of gold and rust within the gear's teeth. The dark, smoky spots along the inner edge mark areas of low cluster density, while the wispy outer tendrils represent trails of roots escaping the central chaotic attractor, fading into the black void.

pages.title: Wreath
pages.text: A blazing, jagged wreath of hot pink, crimson, and pale green encircles a delicate radial sunburst. The central core is a perfect dark void, from which fine, thread-like rays shoot outward, meeting the turbulent, flame-like outer ring. Two prominent flares sweep upward like horns, giving the structure an aggressive, organic symmetry. Thirty-five roots per solve from the poly_1 function are mapped around the unit circle and pushed through the coeff2 transform, while a reversal folds the coefficient vector back on itself. The underlying math—a mix of fractional-power sines, cosines, and logarithmic imaginary terms—creates the chaotic, billowing edges of the outer ring, resolved by the multi-threaded Aberth solver. The image is colored by an averaged metric of the real part of the first parameter and a clusteriness score, both clipped at a tight 0.1 percent to highlight the densest root packings. Finally, the wild fauvism tri-palette paints the high-density regions in vivid pinks and reds, leaving the sparse inner rays glowing in pale green against the black void.

pages.title: Gilded Starflower
pages.text: A five-pointed starburst of sweeping, translucent ribbons in gold and lavender radiates from a tight, intricate floral core against an ink-black void. The distinct five-fold symmetry is explicitly carved by the star parameter transform, while the roots3 and roots6 mappings fracture the smooth sweeps into delicate, overlapping bands that resemble folded silk. The poly_743 function's heavy use of trigonometric and exponential terms weaves the sweeping curves, which are further twisted by a power coefficient transform and a Moebius distortion. Resolved by the Aberth-Ehrlich multi-threading solver, the roots are colored by the t1_re metric, which maps the real component of the first parameter to the tri-ink-gold-lavender palette. This paints the outer ribbons in luminous gold and soft lavender, while the deep ink tones recede seamlessly into the dark background, leaving the delicate tendrils suspended in space.

pages.title: Ember Crest
pages.text: A floating, fiery crest hovers above a sweeping crescent, both rendered in striated bands of rust, gold, and pale peach against a pitch-black void. The central shield-like form is hollow, edged with sharp, thorn-like protrusions and looping finials at its poles, while the detached lower arc curves like a broad scythe. These structures emerge from the poly_598 function, which builds twenty-six complex coefficients using a mix of logarithmic scaling and trigonometric oscillations. The coefficient array is flipped by a reversal transform before being resolved by the Aberth-Ehrlich root-finding algorithm. The spdl and lsp parameter transforms warp the input grid, pulling the root clusters into these distinct, separated bodies. Finally, the t1_re metric maps the real component of the primary input parameter to the long Marvel Ironman palette, painting the fine moiré interference patterns in brilliant metallic hues of armor and ember.

pages.title: Moebius Shuriken
pages.text: Four sharp, scythe-like petals of bright gold and lavender radiate from a dense, swirling vortex, set against a backdrop of dark, sweeping spiral bands. A singular luminous arc whips across the upper left quadrant, echoing the curvature of the central bloom. This intricate structure emerges from the poly_744 function, where ten roots per solve are calculated by the aberth_mt solver across fifteen thousand iterations. The striking symmetry and sweeping background arcs are carved by a sequence of parameter transforms—roots3, roots6, and a moebius mapping—that fracture and fold the smooth input space into sharp, overlapping domains. The t1_re metric evaluates the real component of the first parameter, mapping it to the tri_ink_gold_lavender palette to paint the outer blades in vibrant gold and the dense inner core in deep purples and whites. Inside the function, high-degree polynomial terms and trigonometric coefficients twist the central roots into a tight, luminous knot against the ink-black void.

pages.title: Benthic Carapace
pages.text: A symmetrical, bio-mechanical carapace rendered in luminous teal and gold, resembling an ornate alien mask or a cross-section of a deep-sea organism. A central, jagged mandala of amber teeth is flanked by two glowing ocular nodes, all encased within a smooth, translucent cyan membrane. Thirty-five roots per solve sweep the unit circle, their coefficients warped by a power transform that cubes the values and a reversal operation that folds the sequence back on itself. The poly_1 base function injects logarithmic and trigonometric interference, producing the intricate, crystalline structures in the core. The multi-threaded Aberth solver resolves these heavily distorted polynomials, while the proximity metric—clipped at a tight 0.1 percent—illuminates the densest root clusters in brilliant gold. The reef palette maps these high-density regions to warm amber and the sparser, sweeping outer shells to deep oceanic teal.

pages.title: Crimson Star Turbine
pages.text: Six massive, flared petals of crimson and pale violet radiate from a central black void, resembling a stylized blossom or the glowing exhaust of a starship engine. The inner perimeter of the void is studded with a delicate ring of small, curled nodes, each a miniature red-and-white vortex. Thirty-five roots per solve are generated by the poly_452 function, whose coefficients are shaped by a complex interplay of trigonometric and logarithmic terms. The coefficient vector is then pushed through a sequence of transforms—a reversal, an inverse square power, and a second reversal—that stretches and fractures the root cloud into these six distinct, striated beams. The shelliness metric, clipped at a tight 0.1 percent, highlights the concentric layering of the roots, rendering the fine, hair-like filaments that run along the length of each petal. Finally, the tri_scientific_red_blue palette maps the structural density, painting the dense inner nodes in deep ruby and the broad, sweeping outer edges in cool, luminous violet.

pages.title: Mint Turbine
pages.text: Six sweeping, fan-like petals radiate from a dark central void, their surfaces striated like pleated silk or the bristles of a brush. Thirty-five roots per solve from the poly_452 function are pushed through a sequence of coefficient transforms—a reversal, an inverse square power, and a final reversal—flaring the geometry outward into broad, distinct wedges. A complex scoring metric anchored by shelliness and angular separation highlights the fibrous texture of the fans, painting them in the pale mint, teal, and faint gold of the Washington stripe palette. Along the inner perimeter, the root clusters form intricate, beaded nubs and isolated droplets, a delicate filigree that contrasts with the smooth, sweeping lines of the outer flares.

pages.title: Bauhaus Jade Wreath
pages.text: A jagged, marbled wreath of jade green, pale yellow, and soft orange surrounds a dark central void. Thin, precise golden filaments form a geometric web within the hollow core and sweep outward into faint, intersecting circular arcs that frame the organic structure. Seventy roots per solve are generated by the poly_29 function, which weaves complex exponentials, logarithms, and angular terms into a dense 71-element coefficient array. The inputs are driven through unit circle and exponential parameter transforms, tracing the sweeping outer boundaries, while a reversal coefficient transform folds the polynomial back on itself to create the jagged, taffy-like interior. The Aberth solver resolves the roots simultaneously, and the clusteriness metric evaluates their local density. Areas where roots pack tightly together are illuminated by the long Bauhaus pastel palette, rendering the chaotic folds in smooth, marbled tones against the black void.

pages.title: Inferno Guilloché
pages.text: A luminous, scalloped ring floats against a pitch-black void, its surface woven from thousands of sweeping, moiré-like interference lines. Glowing yellow nodes and deep, shadow-like voids punctuate the band, resembling jewels set into an ornate purple and orange crown. Two small, semi-detached droplets pinch the inner rim at the top and bottom. This intricate structure arises from the g4 polynomial function, solved for twenty-four roots per pixel using the multi-threaded Aberth solver. The sweeping, circular striations are a direct result of the rtheta parameter transform, which warps the input grid into polar coordinates before evaluating the cubic coefficient terms. The composite metric—blending root proximity, nearest-neighbor variation, and phase—maps the structural density of the root cloud, while the inferno palette paints the tightly packed clusters in blinding white-hot yellows and the sparser regions in deep violet. An autolevels pass stretches the final contrast, ensuring the fine, spirographic threads stand out sharply against the dark background.

pages.title: Modular Visage
pages.text: A symmetrical, ornate mask of marbled teal, amber, and gold dominates the dark canvas, its central voids resembling the hollow eyes and mouth of an ancient reliquary. Seventy roots per solve are generated by the poly_180 function, which builds its coefficients using repeating modular powers and an expanding logarithmic envelope. The unit circle and exponential parameter transforms sweep the domain, while a ten-percent reversal fold reflects the coefficient vector, enforcing the structure's striking bilateral symmetry. The multi-threaded Aberth solver resolves the complex polynomial, and the clusteriness metric maps where the roots pack most densely, highlighting the intricate, marbled filigree. Finally, the long Bauhaus pastel palette fills these dense clusters with vivid teal and warm gold, leaving the rootless regions as deep, shadowy voids.

pages.title: Gilded Lavender Mandala
pages.text: A radiant mathematical mandala constructed from sweeping, translucent ribbons of gold and lavender. The composition centers on a tight, ink-dark core resembling a crushed rose, surrounded by a dense, textured annulus. This inner disc is bordered by a ring of intricate, repeating knot-like motifs, beyond which large arcs of golden filaments spiral outward into the void. Thirty-five roots per solve are generated by the poly_594 function, where trigonometric and logarithmic terms introduce the periodic scaling that manifests as the distinct floral boundary ring. The input space is warped by rtheta and cube parameter transforms, while the rev and pow coefficient transforms stretch and fold the polynomial space into these sweeping, overlapping ribbons. The aberth_mt solver resolves the roots, and the clusteriness metric at a tight 0.1 percent clip highlights where the nearest neighbors pack most densely. The tri_ink_gold_lavender palette completes the illusion, painting the dense clusters in bright gold, the sweeping arcs in soft lavender, and the empty space in deep ink.
